summary: labelbook is a standard-library-only Python package that stamps every proposed label with a provenance record (maker kind and identifiers, inputs with sha256 content hashes, code version, time), appends every review decision as an immutable event ordered by a sequence number assigned inside a file lock, and derives state through one shared fold that owns the status vocabulary. Lineage queries (source_of, made_by, acceptance) all read maker fields through a single matcher, and exports are themselves stamped creating paths: plain {"item","label"} rows plus a sidecar bound to the bytes by a content hash that names the exported label ids and their makers. Everything lives in one directory as JSON lines beside a schema.json, so a second Ledger on the same directory sees the same state.

pattern_mapping.Provenance record: labelbook/provenance.py: stamp() returns {kind, ids, inputs[{ref,hash,size,mtime}], version, at}; stored on every line of labels.jsonl via labelbook/model.py: Artefact
pattern_mapping.Stamper: labelbook/provenance.py: stamp() — called by Ledger.add_label for labels and by provenance.stamp_program() in Ledger.export (exports are creating paths too)
pattern_mapping.Schema: labelbook/schema.py: build_schema()/ensure_schema() write schema.json (fields, units, allowed makerKinds, decisions, statusOf, decided, accepting, foldVersion, policy.anonymous) beside the data; check_maker_kind()/check_decision() enforce every allowed-value list at creation
pattern_mapping.Lineage queries: labelbook/lineage.py: source_of(), made_by(), acceptance(), exclude_from(); ledger.source_of / made_by / acceptance / unstamped delegate to them
pattern_mapping.Maker matcher: labelbook/lineage.py: matches() plus field_value() — the only place that knows provenance layout; used by made_by, acceptance and export exclusion
pattern_mapping.Decision event: labelbook/ledger.py: Ledger.decide() builds {seq, label_id, decision, actor, at, reason, new_label}; undo is one of them
pattern_mapping.Decision log: decisions.jsonl, appended by labelbook/storage.py: append_under_lock() — one os.write with O_APPEND under flock, seq allocated inside the same lock
pattern_mapping.Fold: labelbook/folding.py: fold() owns STATUS_OF/status vocabulary, the label in force (last live correction else original), undo marking, and returns (states, problems) with FOLD_VERSION; Ledger.state/acceptance/export read only through it
pattern_mapping.Locked append: labelbook/storage.py: file_lock() (flock + thread lock) and append_record()/append_under_lock(); ids from provenance.new_id() (uuid4), never max+1
pattern_mapping.Export + sidecar: labelbook/ledger.py: Ledger.export() + labelbook/exporting.py: save_stamped()/load_stamped() — content hash binds the sidecar, carries names each exported label's maker

notes_applied: Note 1 (stamping impossible to forget): Artefact's constructor refuses a provenance record without a kind, add_label is the only label-creating path and always stamps, exports are stamped and logged in exports.jsonl, and lines without provenance read back as kind: unknown and are listed by Ledger.unstamped().
Note 3 (undo is an event, order is a sequence number): undo marks the latest live decision undone and history keeps it; fold sorts by seq, never by clock.

Note 4 (define the label in force, test it as laws): corrections overlay the original, the label in force is the last live correction else the original, status from the last live decision; tests/test_fold_laws.py checks the laws plus 120 random sequences against an independent reference model.

Note 5 (one fold owns the vocabulary): labelbook/folding.py is the only mapping from decision to status and from live decisions to label; unknown decisions and 'correct without new_label' are reported with the event and foldVersion, never guessed or folded as rejections.

Note 6 (match makers in one place): matches()/field_value() in labelbook/lineage.py back made_by, acceptance and export exclusion; maker identifiers win over stamp fields with the same name (e.g. a maker's own 'version').

Note 7 (several writers need atomic appends and collision-free ids): uuid4 ids plus one os.write with O_APPEND under flock (and a thread lock); seq allocated under the same lock; tests/test_concurrency.py runs 4 forked processes writing 100 labels and 40 decisions and checks no id or seq is shared.
Note 8 (record who decided, unless policy forbids): decide() refuses a missing or blank actor with ValueError, and schema.json records policy.anonymous = false with a note about roles/pseudonyms.
Note 9 (schema beside the data, enforce the lists): schema.json is written into the ledger directory and read back; unknown maker kinds and decisions raise ValueError at creation.

Note 10 (bind a sidecar to its content and to the labels it carries): <export>.provenance.json holds contentHash of the exact bytes, the export's provenance, and carries[{id, item, maker{kind, ids}, at}]; load_stamped() treats a missing or hash-mismatched sidecar as unstamped.
Note 11 (hash inputs that may change): each input is recorded as {ref, sha256 hash, size, mtime}; a missing file is recorded with null hash rather than a bare path.
tests: 46 tests in 4 modules (test_api.py 25, test_fold_laws.py 11, test_export.py 9, test_concurrency.py 2) covering the public interface, error cases, lineage queries, fold laws against a reference model, export sidecars and four concurrent processes; last run: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -> Ran 46 tests, OK.
chapter_feedback: The chapter's participant table and sketch were directly translatable into modules; the 'one fold, one matcher, one stamper' notes made the boundaries obvious and checkable, which is the most useful part of the chapter.

It left me guessing on one point the task needs: whether artefacts the system itself creates (exports) may use a maker kind outside person/agent/detector. I kept 'program' in the schema's makerKinds but restricted add_label to the task's three kinds, which is a decision the chapter does not make.

The chapter's acceptance formula divides by count(decided), so a maker value whose labels are all pending is undefined; I chose to report 0.0 instead of omitting the key, and documented it — a small ambiguity in the sketch.

It does not say what error semantics decide() should have for an unknown label id (the fold merely reports 'event for unknown artefact'). I raise ValueError at write time and keep the fold's problem reporting for foreign/corrupt logs.

Reading and writing the same directory concurrently is covered only by note 7; the chapter does not mention that read order between artefact log and decision log matters for avoiding phantom problems, which I had to reason about myself.

The named laws in note 4 ('correct then accept keeps the correction', 'undoing a correction restores the one before', 'replay gives equal state') were the most valuable lines in the chapter: they became three tests plus a reference model, and no law broke in this build.
